finalText:
**Both pull changes from one branch into another. They differ in what your history looks like after.**

Merge adds one new commit that joins the two lines. Every old commit stays exactly where it was.

Rebase replays your commits on top of the other branch. They become new commits with new IDs.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Merge
    A1(A) --> B1(B) --> C1(C) --> M(merge)
    B1 --> D1(D) --> E1(E) --> M
  end
  subgraph Rebase
    A2(A) --> B2(B) --> C2(C) --> D2("D'") --> E2("E'")
  end
```

Reach for rebase on your own branch, before anyone else has it. You get a straight line and an easier review.

Reach for merge once the branch is shared or pushed. Rewriting commits other people already pulled will break their copy.
